notes.meaning: Hannah bursts into a song of praise, thanking God for answering her prayer and giving her a son. Her horn being exalted means God restored her strength and dignity after she had been shamed for being childless. She is not just happy about having a baby, but rejoices in the Lord Himself who rescued her from distress. When God answers our cries, our highest praise belongs to Him.

Hannah declares that the Lord alone is holy, which means completely pure and set apart from all evil. No other gods truly exist, and no one else can offer a firm foundation like the God of Israel. Calling God a Rock shows that He is strong, reliable, and an unchanging place of safety.

Hannah warns arrogant people to stop boasting and speaking with pride. The Lord sees and understands everything, and He weighs every human action to judge its true motives. Those who think they are superior should remember that God knows what is in their hearts.

Human strength can fail in an instant, while those who are weak receive strength from God. Powerful warriors often see their weapons shattered, but people who stumble are given new power to stand. Real security comes from the Lord rather than from human might.

Hannah describes how God turns everyday human fortunes upside down. People who once had plenty of food are forced to work for a simple meal, while the starving are filled and hunger no more. A woman who could not have children receives a full household, while a woman who boasted of many children grows weak and lonely.

The Lord holds ultimate authority over life and death. He brings people down to Sheol, the realm of the dead or deep despair, and He can raise them back up again. No hopeless situation is beyond His power to revive and restore.

Riches and poverty are entirely in God's hands. He brings down the proud and lifts up the lowly whenever He chooses. This reminds us to stay humble in times of abundance and to trust God during hard seasons.

God lifts the poorest and most despised people out of the dirt and seats them with rulers and princes. He has full authority to do this because the whole earth belongs to Him and rests on foundations He created. Nothing in all creation happens outside of His sovereign rule.

The Lord protects the steps of those who love and trust Him, keeping them from slipping into ruin. In contrast, wicked people who fight against Him are silenced in darkness and failure. No one can ever succeed or find real safety by relying only on their own power.

Those who oppose the Lord will be shattered when He judges the entire earth. Hannah looks ahead to the king God will choose, speaking of the anointed one, or Messiah, God's specially chosen ruler. This points forward to King David, and ultimately to Jesus Christ, who conquers all enemies.

After their time of worship, Elkanah went home to Ramah, leaving young Samuel behind at Shiloh. Even though Samuel was still a boy, he began assisting in the service of the Lord under the direction of Eli the priest. Young people can serve and please God right where they are.

Eli's sons were corrupt and worthless men who had no real respect for the Lord. Even though they worked as priests and knew religious laws, their hearts did not know or love God. Growing up around holy things does not automatically make a person godly.

Eli's sons created their own selfish habits instead of following God's law for sacrifices. When people boiled the meat for their sacred fellowship meals, a servant would plunge a three-pronged fork into the pot and claim whatever it pulled up for the priests. By doing this, they stole food that belonged to the worshippers who came to Shiloh.

The priests demanded raw meat even before the fat had been burned on the altar for the Lord. When worshippers asked them to let God have His share first, the servant threatened to take the meat by force. This showed that the priests cared more about roasting fine food for themselves than honoring the Lord's altar.

The sin of these young men was terrible in God's eyes because they treated His sacred offerings with contempt. Their greedy behavior disgusted the people and made them hate coming to the sanctuary to worship. Leaders carry a heavy responsibility because their misconduct can turn others away from God.

In contrast to Eli's sons, young Samuel served the Lord with a pure heart. He wore a linen ephod, which was a special sleeveless vest worn during sacred duties. Even as a child, Samuel showed devotion to holy work.

Each year, Hannah lovingly made a small robe for Samuel and brought it when she came with her husband to offer the annual sacrifice. Even though she had given Samuel to the tabernacle, she never stopped caring for him as a mother. Her faithful love supported him as he grew up in God's house.

Eli would bless Elkanah and Hannah, asking the Lord to give them more children in place of the boy they had dedicated to the sanctuary. After receiving this blessing, the parents returned to their home. Dedicating our treasures to God never leaves us empty-handed.

The Lord showed favor to Hannah, and she gave birth to three more sons and two daughters. Meanwhile, the boy Samuel continued to grow in wisdom and character in the presence of the Lord. God proved Himself faithful to reward Hannah's generous heart.

Eli was now very old and learned about the shameful crimes his sons were committing against all Israel. He also heard that they were sleeping with the women who served at the entrance to the tabernacle. Their actions polluted the very place where God's holiness was meant to be honored.

Eli confronted his sons about the terrible reports everyone was bringing to him. He warned them that their wickedness was causing the Lord's people to fall into sin. However, Eli only gave them a gentle talk instead of removing them from the priesthood as a judge should have done.

Eli warned his sons that while an ordinary judge can settle a dispute between two men, no human mediator can step in when someone directly defies the Lord. Even so, the sons refused to listen to their father's rebuke. Because they had stubbornly persisted in evil, the Lord resolved to bring judgment and death upon them.

differ.view: God sovereignly determined to withhold repentance and purposed their death as an act of divine judgment.
God purposed their destruction because they had persistently and willfully chosen to reject repentance.

notes.meaning: While Eli's sons sank into deeper wickedness, young Samuel continued to grow in both physical size and spiritual grace. He gained the favor and love of both the Lord and the people around him. This description looks ahead to how Jesus would grow up in favor with God and man.

An unnamed prophet, called a man of God, arrived to deliver a stern warning to Eli. The prophet reminded Eli how God had first made Himself known to his forefather Aaron when the Israelites were still slaves in Egypt. Remembering God's past mercy shows how serious it is to disregard His commands.

The Lord reminded Eli that He had chosen Aaron's family out of all Israel to serve as His priests. They were given the sacred duties of making offerings, burning incense, and wearing the ephod, along with receiving plenty of food from the sacrifices. God had given them great honor and everything they needed to live well.

God asked Eli why his family treated the holy sacrifices with disrespect by trampling on them. He charged Eli with honoring his sons more than God, because Eli allowed them to steal the choicest parts of the offerings to make themselves fat. Putting family approval above God's law is a dangerous form of rebellion.

The Lord stated that although He had promised Eli's family would serve Him continually, that promise required faithful obedience. God announced a permanent rule of His kingdom: He will honor those who honor Him, but those who despise Him will be brought low. True honor comes only through faithfulness to the Lord.

God warned Eli that He was going to cut off the strength and authority of his family line. The phrase cutting off his strength means taking away their power and influence as priests. In addition, no man in Eli's household would live long enough to reach old age.

Eli was told that he would witness distress and calamity in God's dwelling place, even while Israel experienced blessings. The judgment that no one in his family would ever reach old age is repeated to show that this decree was certain. Sin in spiritual leadership brings grief to both God's house and future generations.

Any descendant of Eli who survived would remain only to see the family's misery and weep with grief of heart. The members of his family line would die early in the prime of life. This warning made it clear that the former glory of Eli's household would completely vanish.

God gave Eli an immediate sign to prove that this entire judgment would come to pass: his two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, would both die on the very same day. Because they had sinned together at the sanctuary, they would perish together in battle. This sign began the fulfillment of God's word against Eli's house.

The Lord promised to raise up a faithful priest who would do what was in God's own heart and mind. God would build an enduring priestly family for him that would serve before His anointed king forever. This promise was fulfilled partly in Zadok under King Solomon, and points ultimately to Jesus Christ, the eternal High Priest.

Any survivors from Eli's family line would eventually become so poor that they would beg the new high priest for a tiny coin or a scrap of bread. They would plead for even the lowest job around the sanctuary just to have enough food to survive. The family that once took the best meat by force would end up begging for a single crust.
